# NOTES (both books; keep apart)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE ROMANCE OF GOLDEN STAR (George Griffith; 1897 F.V. White; illus. Alfred Pearse)

**Frontispiece/epigraph:** Prophecy of Vilcaroya-Inca and Golden Star, his sister-bride: a Son of the Sun who, with a pure virgin of his own holy blood, passes through the Gate of Death, shall cast out the Oppressor, raise the Rainbow Banner above the Golden Throne of the Incas. Contents: Prologue (I His Highness the Mummy; II A Physiological Experiment); Ch I Back Through the Shadows; II Brothers of the Blood; III In the Hall of Gold; IV The Sister Stars; V How Djama Did His Work; VI The Waking of Golden Star; VII In the Throne-Room of Yupanqui; VIII How the Soul of Golden Star Came Back; IX The Treachery of Djama; X On the Rodadero; XI How We Took the City of the Sun; XII Queen and Crown; XIII How Djama Paid His Debt; XIV The Re-kindling of the Sacred Fire.

**Prologue I (London, Maida Vale, Prof. Martin Lamson's house):** Lamson = archaeologist of South American antiquities, just back from Peru/Bolivia. Dr Laurens Djama = physiologist, ~32, slender, olive skin, black hair, deep blue-black eyes, Eastern origin; saved Lamson from calentura in Panama five years earlier. Mummy: Inca prince, lying at full length, hands crossed on breast, face bronze, dull brown hair, aquiline features, not embalmed (no evisceration) and not sitting-posture (anomalies). Lamson found it four days' ride west of Cuzco, near Abancay road, in a circular valley with a lake, behind mortarless masonry; he sent arriero Patricio to village for supplies; found chamber with Vicuna skins; shipped via Cuzco, Sicuani, Arequipa, Mollendo. Djama proposes experiment, Mephistopheles bargain (half of treasures). Djama takes mummy to laboratory at Brondesbury Park.

**Prologue II:** Week later, telegram/note "Come round to the laboratory and make a new acquaintance who will yet be an old one." Vilcaroya revived; Lamson faints. Djama's sister Ruth (Joyful Star) to nurse; cover story: patient from Oriental Home, Whitechapel. Vilcaroya speaks Quichua ("Cori-Coyllur, Nustallipa, Nusta mi!" = "Golden Star, my princess, my darling!"). Vilcaroya: 1532, after Atahuallpa captured at Cajamarca, Huascar slain; feast of Raymi; death-bridal with Golden Star in Sanctuary of the Sun. Promises treasure for her restoration.

**Ch I Back Through the Shadows (Vilcaroya narrates):** Son of Huayna-Capac; dreams of Golden Star; awakens 1897-era. Ruth named "Cusi-Coyllur" (Joyful Star) after Ollantay's maiden. Francis Hartness: English captain, ~30, tall, blue eyes, golden hair/beard, met at Panama square. Route: Panama → steamer south → Arequipa (Charchani, Pichu-Pichu, Misti) → Sicuani → Cacha, Piquillacta → Cuzco (Plain of the Oracle). Vilcaroya vows vengeance.

**Ch II Brothers of the Blood:** Village San Sebastian (2 leagues south of Cuzco). Ullullo (old Indian, friend, helps). Tupac Rayca (chief; great-grandson of Tupac-Amaru), homage with hoe. Twenty men of Blood. Hacienda 3 leagues west, price 20,000 soles (£2,000). Djama: "His Highness... unlock one of those treasure-houses." Hartness: first to unlock is his wife. Vilcaroya: "Let the house be bought." Joyful Star: "Your sister!" horrified; will go back to England. Hartness's speech: sister-marriage unacceptable. Vilcaroya's farewell to Hartness ("Vilcaroya Inca is your friend").

**Ch III In the Hall of Gold:** Vilcaroya disguised; Djama pays Ullullo $10 to spy; Vilcaroya leads Djama blindfolded via Rodadero, Sayacusca (Tired Stone), cleft with broken stairway, copper chain releases water. Secret passages (50 steps, 40 paces); Vilcaroya dons Huascar's robes (Llautu). Hall of Gold: golden plates, gold bar pyramid, Sun images with diamond eyes. Tupac and Children of Blood hail him. Djama sworn to silence; threatened. Gold sold via coca bales; hacienda bought; household at hacienda; left 15th day for Golden Star's resting place.

**Ch IV The Sister Stars:** Five-day journey; Saljantai, Umantai (snow peaks), Lima Tambo, Rio de la Banca, Apurimac bridge. Two twin peaks; tunnel with pillar lock behind Tupac; Golden Star's tomb by black cliff beside lake. Vilcaroya confesses love for Ruth, not Golden Star; Hartness approaches. Vilcaroya opens tomb; Ruth and Golden Star resemble each other. Ruth kisses Golden Star's brow.

**Ch V How Djama Did His Work:** Djama locks himself with Golden Star. Vilcaroya woken at night; sees Golden Star in "borderland." Djama reveals he loves her; demands her; Vilcaroya threatens with dagger; demands Djama give Ruth to him. Djama yields ("My sister for your sister").

**Ch VI The Waking of Golden Star:** Ruth pleads; Djama relents. Ruth: "no one can give an English girl away." Golden Star awakens with kiss from Ruth; cannot yet speak; child-mind. Vilcaroya and Hartness make alliance ("brothers-in-arms, rivals in love"). Peru civil war, Government/President; treasury empty.

**Ch VII In the Throne-Room of Yupanqui:** Golden Star (17 apparent age) child-like. Ruth nurses her. Djama asks reward; Vilcaroya requires oath of secrecy witnessed in Hall of Gold. Djama suggests Golden Star go to England with Ruth. Golden Star meets Vilcaroya in garden; she shrinks from Djama ("Evil Eyes" later). Ruth and Vilcaroya in garden; treasure-house under Sacsahuaman shown. Throne-room of Yupanqui (golden effigy, mummies of 20 Incas, silver seats). Vilcaroya proposes to Ruth on throne; she is to sit beside him. Ruth: "Your queen is not crowned yet."

**Ch VIII How the Soul of Golden Star Came Back:** 60 heads of Ayllo families assembled. Vilcaroya reveals Golden Star, declares Joyful Star his Coya; Hartness named war-chief. Golden Star's soul returns when Llautu touches brow: "Have they awakened us, my lord?" Ruth and Golden Star share a room. Djama told to go; Djama and professor (Lamson) prisoners. Bronze doors; secret triangle-stone; 1,200 paces gallery; revolving stone; Fortress outside. Hartness's rifles on ridge ready for attack.

**Ch IX The Treachery of Djama:** Tupac's men; Spanish officer (Governor Prada's son, Coronel Prada) captured in Hall. Djama betrayed Vilcaroya to Governor Antonio Prada for half the gold. Djama's attempt on Golden Star; Djama thrust into golden cell (with Spaniard). Lamson chooses to stay; Hartness's advice on prisoners. Golden walls built; Djama and Prada imprisoned.

**Ch X On the Rodadero:** Ruth told of brother's treachery; Vilcaroya promises life. Anahuac reports Prada to bring 200 soldiers, dynamite, to Sayacusca. Password "Vilcaroya." Hartness, disguised, kills sentry scenario; Vilcaroya kills Spanish officer with knife. Hartness takes sentry prisoners.

**Ch XI How We Took the City of the Sun:** Trap at water-cavern; Governor and officers yield at steps; Hartness takes Governor prisoner; Vilcaroya takes sword at Inca's Seat. Cuzco taken: Hartness commands machine-guns (Gatlings/Maxims) from Cuartel. Governor's proclamation; Hartness made Governor of Cuzco.

**Ch XII Queen and Crown:** Ruth "Your queen"; Djama insults from cell. Gold distributed (2 oz each). Golden Throne set before cathedral; Rainbow Banner raised at sunrise; Vilcaroya proclaims himself Inca.

**Ch XIII How Djama Paid His Debt:** Djama brought before throne; Djama shoots from soldier's rifle at Vilcaroya; kills Ullullo (who dies behind throne). Djama poisons/chokes himself (breath held), dies. Hartness steps in.

**Ch XIV The Re-kindling of the Sacred Fire:** Empire restored; Lima taken; Feast of Raymi. Tupac-Rayca made Villac-Umu. Golden Star holds Sacred Fleece; fire ignites. Marriage-font (wine and water) between Vilcaroya and Joyful Star; Hartness and Golden Star at font. Footnote: Church of Santo Domingo (Temple of Sun site). Book ends with Lamson's "Great book" co-written with Hartness and Ruth.

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE TEMPLETON CASE (Victor L. Whitechurch; 1924 Edward J. Clode, NY)

**Chapters:** I Reginald Templeton Comes to Marsh Quay; II The Visit to the Opposite Shore; III A Terrible Discovery; IV What Canon Fittleworth Found on the "Firefly"; V Detective-Sergeant Colson Discovers Clues; VI Colson is Baffled; VII The Inquest; VIII Winnie Cotterill Pays a Visit to Frattenbury; IX The Cigar Band; X Harold Grayson is Detained; XI The Canon's Cigars; XII Fresh Evidence; XIII Isaac Moss Explains; XIV Reginald Templeton's Letter; XV Detective-Sergeant Colson's Deductions; XVI Mr. Proctor Upsets Matters; XVII New Theories; XVIII Sir James Perrivale's Story; XIX Colson Makes an Appointment; XX Colson's "Imagination"; XXI Final Solution of the Problem.

**Setting:** Marsh Quay, estuary near Frattenbury (cathedral city, 2 miles north); "Mariner's Arms" inn run by Mrs. Yates (widow, 6 yrs); schooner *Lucy* (Tom Gale, crew/cook; "captain" and "mate" at Frattenbury). Opposite shore: wood, house of Isaac Moss (Jewish diamond dealer, 53 Compton Avenue, Brondesbury; office 13a Hatton Garden; "Fairview"). Canon Fittleworth lives in the Close.

**Ch I:** Saturday, October. Tom Gale sees cutter yacht *Firefly* arrive, anchored at Marsh Quay, with Reginald Templeton (~50, moustache, iron-grey beard, tanned) and crew Jim Webb (Salcombe, Mr. Jefferies' boats). Art lodger Harold Grayson (~25, fair, clean-shaven, blue eyes) in bar parlour; learns Templeton from Africa; Grayson gives cigar to Tom Gale. Grayson watches Templeton.

**Ch II:** Templeton rows dinghy across estuary to Moss's shore; Grayson watches; Tom Gale identifies Moss. Templeton dines at Canon's (cousin), leaves ~8:30 for Frattenbury. Night dark.

**Ch III:** Sunday morning: Webb finds Templeton dead, stabbed in back (dagger wound, heart), face down in cabin. Mrs. Yates tells Mr. Proctor (bald, egg-headed, velveteen jacket, retired cigar merchant, nephew Phil, 15). Superintendent Norton; Colson (Detective-Sergeant, plainclothes, shrewd grey eyes). Doctor: death after midnight, probably before. Grayson had left early by bicycle.

**Ch IV:** Canon Thomas? (Canon Charles Fittleworth, pince-nez; daughter Doris; wife). Coroner Francis Norwood (solicitor, hatchet face, mutton-chops, unmarried, stiff). Canon finds red-and-gold cigar band in cabin, pockets it. Canon's Spanish friend De Garcia sent special Cuban brand cigars. Canon says Templeton mentioned carrying valuable thing; going to Frattenbury to call on someone. Moss had left for London Sunday morning. Canon takes band home, compares with box.

**Ch V:** Colson sets up at Marsh Quay. Gadsden (constable). Simmonds saw Templeton walk to Frattenbury. Colson matches shoe prints on field path (right side going in; reverse going back) and walking-stick ferrule (Alpine, square, 3/8 inch). Canon's Alpine stick. Letter typewritten "I shall be at home... Saturday evening after 8.30." Blotting pad: "see you on Saturday afternoon" / "R. Templeton". Diamond in chamois bag (pea-sized). Stick found under dinghy stern seat (not Templeton's). Colson orders Peters to watch.

**Ch VI:** Blake (tobacconist) copies stick with new ferrule. Mrs. Colson (wife, Bob). Colson swaps stick with fake; Proctor paddles to dinghy at night; Colson with red glass signal; Gadsden paddles and leaves. Colson trips on post; canoe thief escapes. Proctor's canoe found stranded; Proctor's nephew Phil. Julier Pass picture (Switzerland).

**Ch VII Inquest:** Held at "Mariner's Arms" bar parlour. Coroner Norwood; foreman Proctor. Witnesses: Webb, doctor, Tom Gale, Superintendent, Canon. Canon produces cigar band; coroner rebukes; band passed round jury, and coroner drops papers. Adjourned to Saturday week. Colson pockets band.

**Ch VIII:** Winnie Cotterill (Winifred; art illustrator; flat in Battersea Park with Maude Wingrave) learns of murder; Templeton was her benefactor ("Uncle"; paid art training). She visits Canon's; Anthony Crosby (lawyer, Crosby & Paxton, 17b Lincoln's Inn Fields) reveals Templeton's will leaves all to Winifred (~£2,000). Templeton's lawsuit with Norwood? (Crosby mentions "other man" bought property). Grayson mentioned; Winnie upset.

**Ch IX:** Colson deductions; Tom Gale gets cigar from Grayson; Colson compares band: same brand. Moss confirmed in London (Hatton Garden). Tyler watches Moss.

**Ch X:** Grayson detained at Linderton (Constable Drake). Chief Constable Major Renshaw. Grayson: father Osmond Grayson, Marlow; lawsuit with Templeton. Crosby confirms. Band brought to Canon.

**Ch XI:** Funeral. Canon's cigar band identification: Canon says band shown is NOT the one; coroner's jury changed it. Mrs. Yates: Grayson didn't have walking stick. Grayson released; dines at Canon's.

**Ch XII:** Chief Constable's plan (kept quiet). Dinner at Norwood's; Dr Hazell, Sir Peter Birchnall, Rev. Alfred Carringford; "Virginian Reefs." Joe Thatcher (poacher) saw man rowing from opposite shore ~12:30–1 a.m. Sunday; motor car stopped near quay. Colson checks Moss's dinghy with green paint.

**Ch XIII:** Moss arrested/explains: agent for Ehbrenstein & Co.; diamonds (32, one missing). Moss rowed out at ~1 a.m. Sunday, found Templeton dead. Fled Sunday morning with wife to Chester Hotel. Moss released. Colson: walking stick too long for Moss.

**Ch XIV:** Crosby tells Winnie Templeton's will; Winnie engaged to Grayson. Templeton's sealed letter: Winnie's real name is Forbes; father Percy Forbes, lawyer, convicted of embezzlement; died at Princetown. Templeton gave Crosby £100 and asked discretion.

**Ch XV:** Colson visits cigar importer in London; Proctor's cupboard of Cuban cigars; Colson's deductions (Templeton killed by person with cigar; walking stick under seat; "A" theory). Proctor's cigar cupboard checked.

**Ch XVI:** Inquest resumed. Postman saw Templeton leave Close ~8:30–9. Moss testifies. Jury wants verdict. Proctor reveals alibi: at Merrifield's (corn merchant) playing bridge until 1:30 a.m.; Merrifield drove him back. Proctor had watched Colson take cigar from cupboard. Crosby examines blotting pad: "EZRA'S ICES" = "EZRA PRICE(S)" or "EZRA GRICE"; "hand over Ezra Grice's confession & proof."

**Ch XVII:** Mrs. Colson's theories: left-handed, tall man. Simmonds recalls Templeton carried stick by middle. Chemist Buckland recalls Ezra Grice (ex-clerk of Norwood). Norwood's whisky; admits Grice was clerk; robbery; Norwood speculating. Dr Hazell buys Virginian Reefs (500 shares). Canon's list; Dean had a cigar box (from Canon).

**Ch XVIII:** Advertisement for Ezra Grice; Crosby's £50 reward offer; Sir James Perrivale (big-game, South Africa) reveals Grice was with Templeton; Grice had broken arm, fever; Templeton left him with Zulu; Grice recovered in Cape Town. Grice to return via boat due Plymouth Dec 8 ("E. G. started from Cape").

**Ch XIX:** Colson learns from Proctor: Jurymen Bailey or Westall probably changed the band. Colson calls Dean (abroad). Crosby researches Forbes case at British Museum. Colson gets Canon's walking-stick; Chief Constable and Superintendent Norton. Grice arrives Plymouth.

**Ch XX:** Colson arrests Francis Norwood at Canon's house: the walking-stick (left-handed; dummy stick used in cleanup). Grice reveals story. Norwood's housekeeper recognised stick.

**Ch XXI:** Grice's story: Norwood embezzled from clients; Grice's perjury; Templeton blackmail plan to get £10,000 from Norwood for Forbes's daughter Winifred. Norwood's appointment, meeting, dagger; he took proofs; killed Templeton; took pocket contents. Norwood hanged himself in cell (braces). Crosby to decide whether to tell Winifred. Canon notes Winifred's sense of having been to Frattenbury.
